steps: Press the tofu between kitchen paper for 5 minutes, then cut into 2cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat and fry the tofu for 4-5 minutes, turning, until golden on most sides.
Push the tofu to one side, add the minced garlic and ginger, and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the mixed stir-fry vegetables and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender.
Pour in the soy sauce, toss everything together for 1 minute, and serve immediately.
Brown the ground turkey in a large pot over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and bell pepper and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the chilli powder and cumin, then add the chopped tomatoes and kidney beans and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, rinse the quinoa and cook in salted water for 12-15 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir the cooked quinoa through the chilli, or serve it alongside, then portion into 6 containers to cool before freezing.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot or slow cooker over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the chilli powder and cumin, then add the chopped tomatoes and kidney beans.
Simmer uncovered for 40 minutes on the stovetop, or on low for 6-8 hours in a slow cooker, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Cook the rice in salted water for 15 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the chilli over the rice, or cool and portion into 6 containers to freeze.
Add the oil to a large pot. Sauté the vegetables and spices in the oil over medium to medium-low heat for 10 minutes or until tender.
Add a few tablespoons of water if the veggies begin sticking to the pot.
Add the remaining ingredients except the cilantro and simmer over medium-low heat, covered, for 30 minutes.
Stir and simmer for an additional 20 to 30 minutes until the veggies are cooked through.
Season with salt and, if more spice is desired, hot sauce or cayenne pepper to taste. Serve sprinkled with the cilantro.
Put the chicken breast, white beans, chopped green chillies, chopped onion, cumin and chicken stock into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours, until the chicken is tender enough to shred easily.
Remove the chicken, shred it with two forks, then stir it back into the pot.
About 20 minutes before serving, cook the rice in salted water until tender, then drain.
Serve the chilli spooned over the rice.
Brown the ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the diced sweet potato and chopped bell pepper and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the chilli powder and cumin, then add the chopped tomatoes.
Cover and simmer for 35-40 minutes on the stovetop, or slow-cook on low for 6-8 hours, until the sweet potato is tender.
Season to taste and serve.
Cut the beef chuck into 3cm chunks and brown in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes for extra flavour (optional).
Put the beef, diced potatoes, sliced carrots, chopped onion, thyme and beef stock into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
Season to taste, then portion into 6 containers to cool before freezing.
Heat a splash of oil in a large pot and sauté the chopped onion for 2-3 minutes.
Add the chicken stock, chopped tomatoes, black beans and corn, then submerge the chicken breast in the liquid.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken, shred with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Squeeze in the lime juice, ladle into bowls, and top with the tortilla strips.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the diced carrot, celery and courgette for 6-8 minutes until softened.
Add the chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the small pasta and cannellini beans, then simmer for 10-12 minutes until the pasta is cooked.
Season to taste and serve hot.
Bring the chicken broth to a simmer in a pot with the sliced carrot and a few slices of ginger, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the shredded chicken breast and simmer for 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Meanwhile, soak or boil the rice noodles according to the packet instructions until tender, then drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle over the hot broth and chicken, and scatter with scallion greens.
Bring a pan of water to the boil and cook the ramen noodles for 2-3 minutes until just tender, then drain and set aside.
Cut the tofu into cubes and slice the mushrooms.
In a separate pan, bring 400ml water to a gentle simmer, add the mushrooms and bok choy, and cook for 3-4 minutes until the bok choy wilts.
Remove from the heat and stir in the miso paste and soy sauce until dissolved — don't let the broth boil once the miso is in, or it loses its flavour.
Add the noodles and tofu to the broth, warm through for 1 minute, and top with sliced scallion.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15-18 minutes until tender, then drain and mash with the oat milk and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a pan and sauté the chopped onion and carrot for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the peas, cooked lentils and tomato paste, and cook for 3-4 minutes until well combined; season to taste.
Spoon the lentil mixture into an ovenproof dish and spread the mashed potato evenly on top.
Bake at 200°C (fan 180°C) for 20 minutes until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the diced carrot, celery and courgette for 6-8 minutes until softened.
Add the chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cooked brown lentils and shredded kale, and simmer for a further 5-6 minutes until the kale wilts and everything is heated through.
Season to taste and serve.
Let the shop-bought dough come to room temperature for 20-30 minutes, then preheat the oven as high as it will go, ideally 240-250°C, with a baking tray or pizza stone inside.
Stretch or roll the dough out on a floured surface into a thin round.
Spread the passata evenly over the dough, leaving a border for the crust.
Tear the mozzarella into pieces and scatter over the top, then drizzle with the olive oil.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake for 8-10 minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Scatter fresh basil leaves over the pizza as soon as it comes out of the oven.
